lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Fill the template for: Does ramp height change how far a car travels?

FEEDBACK
Change height; same car/release; measure distance; safety for cars/ramps; prediction linked to height.

WATCH FOR
A plan without a measure cannot show results clearly.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Complete a full fair-test plan for your chosen question. Get an adult safety OK. Prepare a blank results table for next lesson. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Change height; same car/release; measure distance; safety for cars/ramps; prediction linked to height. Reasoning: I used fair test by attending to plan and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: A plan without a measure cannot show results clearly. Correction: Change height; same car/release; measure distance; safety for cars/ramps; prediction linked to height. Why: the correction restores accurate use of fair test.

Parent: Likely misconception: A plan without a measure cannot show results clearly. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses fair test. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about fair test, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

teach_steps.explain:
Planning a fair test states the question, what you will change, what you will keep the same, what you will measure and how you will stay safe.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
